description:
Registers one message generation and returns immediately with `202 Accepted`. Poll the
status resource named in `Location` (or honour `Retry-After`) until `status` is terminal;
the finished message is embedded in that resource. The API composes text; it does **not**
send it, and it does not replace the recipient's WhatsApp opt-in.

## What the message may say
Every candidate fact about the recipient and the sender carries a tier. The message
**asserts only facts of tier `verified`**. `reported` and `estimated` facts may influence
which angle is chosen but are never stated as fact; `unknown` facts are never mentioned.
The tier of each field is derived from the provenance the record already carries
(field by field, from its source and verification evidence), not chosen by the model.
Personal data - contacts, officers, phone numbers, e-mail addresses, social handles, and,
for a sole trader, the person's own name and address - is **never** asserted. After
generation, code re-checks that each claim in the text maps to `fact_ids` of `verified`
facts; an unsupported claim is removed, or the request fails - it is never shipped.

## Language
The message is written in the language of the **recipient company's website main page**.
There is no caller override. The decision is reported on the result as `language`
(ISO 639-1) and `language_source`. If the homepage language cannot be determined the
request fails with error code `language_undetermined` and the credits are returned;
the language is never guessed.

## Unknown companies
If the recipient or sender company is not yet known, the status passes through
`enriching`, which runs the existing discovery/validation pipeline for that single
domain, then `composing`.

## Cost and balance
There is exactly **one debit, at `POST`**, for the whole generation including any
enrichment. Enrichment never debits again and never changes the balance mid-job; a
generation that ends `failed` for any reason below, or `canceled` before composition
starts, returns that one debit. `402 insufficient_credits` is therefore only ever
returned by `POST`.

## Jurisdiction
Checked at `POST` against what is already known: `422 jurisdiction_excluded`. A company
whose jurisdiction only becomes known **after** enrichment is excluded late: the
generation ends `failed` with `error.error` = `jurisdiction_excluded` and the credits are
returned. The text is never composed for an excluded jurisdiction.

## Validation done before `202`
Invalid body or hostname: `400 invalid_request`. `sender.company_domain` is the sender's own
company domain: the service reads the sender's facts from the knowledge base by it and does not
verify that the caller controls it. When `sender` or `sender.company_domain` is omitted, the caller's
seller profile website is the sender; with no profile website either, the request is `400 invalid_request`
(`sender.company_domain is required when no seller profile website is set`).
Recipient or sender in a policy-excluded
jurisdiction: `422 jurisdiction_excluded`. Insufficient credits: `402
insufficient_credits`. `constraints.max_characters` that no message can meet: `422
max_characters_unmeetable`; when this only shows during composition the generation ends
`failed` with the same code and the credits are returned. `callback_url` must be an `https` URL on a public host: a URL resolving to a
private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast or cloud-metadata address is rejected
with `422 unsafe_url` (the same rule as `odoo_url` on the tenant Odoo endpoint).
The service being temporarily unable to accept work: `503 service_unavailable` with
`Retry-After`; nothing is debited.

## Error codes
Every error uses the surface's single `Error` shape `{error, message, request_id}`.
`error` is a snake_case code: `invalid_request`, `missing_idempotency_key`,
`idempotency_key_reused`, `request_in_flight`,
`jurisdiction_excluded`, `insufficient_credits`, `unsafe_url`, `max_characters_unmeetable`,
`not_cancelable`, `generation_expired`,
`service_unavailable`, and, on a `failed` generation only, the `MessageFailureCode` values:
`insufficient_verified_facts` (too few verified facts exist to write anything true),
`enrichment_failed`, `language_undetermined`, `language_failed`, `claim_verification_failed`,
`jurisdiction_excluded`, `max_characters_unmeetable`, `compose_failed`, `compose_timeout` and
`timed_out`. A `failed` generation always returns its credits.

## Idempotency (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07)
`Idempotency-Key` is **required**. Missing: `400 missing_idempotency_key`. Same key with a
different payload: `422 idempotency_key_reused`. Same key while the original request is
still being processed: `409 request_in_flight`. Same key with the same payload: **`200`**
(not `202`) with the EXISTING resource in its current state (same `id`, no second debit).
A key is remembered for **24 hours** from its first use; after that the same key starts a
new generation.

inputSchema.description: What to write, to whom, from whom. There is NO language field: the message language is the language of the recipient company's website main page, reported on the result. If sender is omitted, the caller's seller profile website is the sender; the profile's offering and description are used as sender facts. If sender.company_domain differs from the profile website, the profile is not used.

callback_url.description: RESERVED. Accepted and stored, but no callback is delivered yet; poll the status resource. Must be an `https` URL on a public host: private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast and cloud-metadata addresses are rejected with `422 unsafe_url` (same rule as `odoo_url` on the tenant Odoo endpoint).

max_characters.description: Bounds the message text only. The email subject has its own fixed cap of 80 characters and is not counted against this limit.

objective.description: What the message should achieve, in the caller's words.

company_domain.description: Lowercase hostname (internationalised names in punycode); no scheme, path or port.

name.description: The person's name, as the caller knows it.

role.description: The person's role at the company.

sender.description: The sender's own company domain. The service reads the sender's facts from the knowledge base by it; ownership is not verified. If sender is omitted, the caller's seller profile website is the sender; the profile's offering and description are used as sender facts. If sender.company_domain differs from the profile website, the profile is not used.

company_domain.description: Lowercase hostname (internationalised names in punycode); no scheme, path or port.
